title: New Vishing Attack Exploits Microsoft Teams and QuickAssist to Deploy .NET Malware

llm.summary: A sophisticated vishing campaign uses social engineering and legitimate Microsoft tools to establish command execution chains, leading to the deployment of multi-stage .NET malware. Threat actors impersonate IT personnel in Microsoft Teams calls, convincing victims to launch Windows Quick Assist, which grants remote access. The attackers then deploy a fileless malware that executes entirely within memory.
llm.attack_summary: The attack begins with social engineering via Microsoft Teams, where the attacker impersonates an IT person and convinces the victim to launch Windows Quick Assist. Once Quick Assist is launched, the attacker gains remote access and redirects the victim to a malicious webpage. The malware is then deployed in multiple stages: first, a .NET Core 8.0 wrapper containing an embedded loader component is executed without disk-based persistence; next, the loader establishes communication with the command and control infrastructure and retrieves an encrypted payload; finally, the decrypted assembly is loaded into running process memory using .NET reflection capabilities.

title: North Korean hackers exploit React2Shell flaw in EtherRAT malware attacks

llm.summary: North Korean hackers exploit React2Shell flaw in EtherRAT malware attacks, targeting 30 organizations across multiple sectors.
llm.attack_summary: The attack chain starts with the exploitation of React2Shell to execute a base64 encoded shell command on the target. The command attempts to download a malicious shell script and loops every 300 seconds until successful. When the script is fetched, it creates a hidden directory in the user's $HOME/.local/share/ location where it downloads and extracts a legitimate Node.js runtime directly from nodejs.org. It then writes an encrypted payload blob and an obfuscated JavaScript dropper that is executed using the downloaded Node binary.

Ransomware gangs turn to Shanya EXE packer to hide EDR killers

llm.title: STAC6565 Spear Phishing Campaign Uses Legitimate Job Search Platforms to Deliver Malware
llm.summary: A new campaign has been discovered that uses legitimate job search platforms to deliver malware. The attackers are targeting human resources personnel with spear phishing emails containing malicious documents disguised as resumes or cover letters.
llm.author: Sophos

content.title: Introduction
content.text: This report describes a new campaign that uses legitimate job search platforms to deliver malware. The attackers are targeting human resources personnel with spear phishing emails containing malicious documents disguised as resumes or cover letters.

content.title: Attack Vector
content.text: The attackers use job search platforms like Indeed, JazzHR, and ADP WorkforceNow to upload the weaponized resumes. The malicious documents are designed to be opened by human resources personnel, who are tricked into thinking they contain legitimate job applications.

content.title: Delivery Chain
content.text: The delivery chain involves several stages: (1) spear phishing email with a malicious document, (2) execution of the payload by running a Windows shortcut that impersonates a PDF, and (3) connection to an external server to download and execute the second-stage payload.

content.title: Malware Analysis
content.text: The malware analyzed in this report is a multi-stage payload delivery chain. The first stage includes a DLL that connects to an external server to download and execute the second-stage payload, which is a standalone binary responsible for connecting to another server and retrieving the third-stage executable alongside a malicious DAT file.

content.title: Recommendations
content.text: To mitigate this threat, organizations should use local ESXi accounts, enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA), implement a strong password policy, segregate the hypervisor's management network from production and general user networks, deploy a jump box to audit admin access, limit access to the control plane, and restrict ESXi management interface access to specific administrative devices.

content.title: Conclusion
content.text: This campaign demonstrates a sophisticated attack strategy that uses legitimate job search platforms to deliver malware. Organizations must remain vigilant in protecting against these types of attacks by implementing robust security measures and staying up-to-date with the latest threat intelligence.
